Kabc030186622019
 In The Court Of Xlvi

Additional Chief Judicial
 Magistrate, Bengaluru.

Present : Lokesha. C.N,
 M.A., Ll.,B.
 Xlvi Addl.C.J.M., Bengaluru.
04th day of August 2025

Complainant: State by - Byatarayanapura Police Station
 (By A.P.P.)
 V/s
 Accused:
 1. Ananda.

S/o. Kumar
 A/a 35 years
 2. Lalitha, W/o. Kumar
 A/a 60 years
 A.1 and A2.

R/o. Kavika Layout
 Mysore road, Bengaluru.

3. Menaka, W/o. Babu
 A/a 40 years
 R/o. Bapuji nagara
 Mysore Road, Bengaluru.
 (By Sri. K.N. Shashidhar., Advocate)
2  C.C.No.6203/2019  JUDGMENT

This is a charge sheet filed by Byatarayanapura Police station against the accused No. 1 to 3 for the offence punishable Under Sections 498(A), 323, 324, 504 R/w Section 34 of IPC.
2.
The case of the prosecution in brief is that, the marriage of the accused No.1 solemnized with Cw.1 at Bengaluru as per their customs.
The marriage of the accused and the complainant was love marriage.

After the marriage the accused No.1 and complainant were residing at Kavika Layout,

1 Mysore road, Bengaluru.
Thereafter, the accused persons without any reason everyday used to quarrel with the complainant by suspecting her character.
The accused used subjected her physical and mental cruelty.
On 26.11.2018 at about 4.30 pm, the accused No.1 abused the complainant with filthy language, assaulted her with hands and glass piece.
On the basis of the complaint given by the Cw.1, the Cw.7 registered a case in Cr.No.526/2018.
Thereafter the Cw.7 having completed the investigation filed charge sheet against accused persons for the aforesaid offences.
3. After filing of the charge sheet, the presence of the accused No. 1 to 3 was secured.

Thereafter the copies of the charge sheet papers furnished to the accused No. 1 to 3 and after hearing both sides,
the charges were framed for the offence punishable under section 498A, 323, 324, 504 R/w C.C.No.6203/2019 Section 34 of IPC.
The accused No. 1 to 3 pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried for the said offences.
4. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No. 1 to 3 the prosecution examined one witnesses as P.W.1 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 & P2.
PW1 being the complainant and being material witness has turned hostile and did not chose to support the case of prosecution.
Hence, the prayer of learned APP to issue summons to remaining witnesses was rejected as no purpose would have been served by examining remaining witnesses.
The statement of accused No. 1 to 3 U/Section 313 of Cr.P.C., was also dispensed with as there were no incriminating circumstances against the accused in the evidence of Pw.1.
Thereafter, I have heard the arguments of both sides and perused the entire record, in the facts and circumstances of the case the following points arises for consideration.

:POINTS:
Point No.1: Whether the prosecution proves an offence punishable Under Section 498(A) R/w Section 34 of IPC against the accused No. 1 to 3 beyond all reasonable doubt?
Point No.2: Whether the prosecution proves an offence punishable Under Section 504 R/w Section 34 of IPC against the accused No. 1 to 3 beyond all reasonable doubt?
Point No.3: Whether the prosecution proves an offence punishable Under Section C.C.No.6203/2019 323 R/w Section 34 of IPC against the accused No. 1 to 3 beyond all reasonable doubt?

Point No.4: Whether the prosecution proves an offence punishable Under Section 324 R/w Section 34 of IPC against the accused No. 1 to 3 beyond all reasonable doubt?
5. Point No.1 to 4: under consideration are answered in the Negative for the following:
REASONS Point No.1 to 4:

2 6.
These points are inter-related; hence I have discussed them together to avoid repetition of facts and evidence.

The PSI of Byatarayanapura police station filed the charge sheet against the accused No. 1 to 3 for the offence punishable under Section 498(A), 323, 324, 504 R/w Section 34 of IPC.
7.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No. 1 to 3, the prosecution examined the complainant as P.W.1.
The PW.1 is the wife of the accused No.1.
The Pw.1 being complainant and material witness has turned hostile to the case of prosecution, as she deposed in her evidence

that,
the she was not subjected any physical and mental cruelty from the accused No. 1 to 3.
The accused No.1 has not assaulted her not abused her with filthy language.
When the Pw.1 went police station at that time the police have obtain the signature of the Pw.1 and she does not know about the contents of the Ex.P.1 & P.2.
The Pw.1 did not lodged any complaint against C.C.No.6203/2019 the accused persons.

Hence, in view of fact that, the Pw.1 herself turned completely hostile to the case of prosecution, the prayer of learned APP to issue summons to remaining witnesses was rejected as no purpose would have been served by examining the remaining witnesses.
The Ld. APP treated the prosecution witness as hostile witness and cross- examined.
In the cross-examination also the Pw.1 did not chose to support the case of the prosecution and deposed the evidence in consonance with the chief examination.
The Pw.1 during the course of cross examination as clearly admitted that the matter was settled between the parties.
Therefore, prosecution has failed to prove the guilty of the accused No. 1 to 3 beyond all reasonable doubt.

Accordingly, I answer point No.1 to 4 in the Negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
Exercising the power under section 248 (1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No. 1 to 3 are acquitted for the offences punishable Under Section 498(A),323, 324, 504 R/w Section 34 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bonds stand cancelled.
